It’s like all I think about is how small and weak I look, even though people at the studio say I’m “fit” or “muscular.” When I look in the mirror, my chest and arms seem tiny, almost like they’re shrinking. It feels unbearable, like everyone must be noticing how scrawny I am.

Most of my day revolves around trying to hide it. I wear oversized hoodies and long sleeves even when it’s hot, and I layer shirts to make my upper body look bigger. If I have to go outside without a jacket, I’ll change outfits over and over until I find something that makes me look less “small.” Sometimes I’m late to meetings with my artist because I’m stuck doing that.

My anxiety is almost entirely about this—how I look, how my body will appear in public, whether people will think I’m pathetic or childish-looking. I keep checking mirrors and comparing myself to the muscular characters we draw, and it just makes the anxiety spike again.

I keep thinking I’m way too scrawny, that no one takes me seriously because I look weak, even though people tell me I look fine or “fit.” I change shirts a few times before going out, wear hoodies even when it’s hot to cover my arms and chest, sometimes a mask or hat so I don’t feel so exposed.
